name: Bajaj Finance Ltd

business.about: Bajaj Finance is mainly engaged in the business of lending. BFL has a diversified lending portfolio across retail, SME and commercial customers with a significant presence in urban and rural India. It also accepts public and corporate deposits and offers variety of financial services products to its customers.(Source : 202003 Annual Report Page No:124)
business.key_points: Business Overview: [1] The company is India's largest private-sector Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) , catering to both individual and business customers through a portfolio of financial products and services. Its offerings span loans, fixed deposits, payments, insurance, and mutual funds through its mobile app, website, and social media, and through its branch network.

calls.tone: Management expressed confidence in strong performance and growth, while acknowledging and strategizing for potential headwinds.
pushback: MSME asset quality deterioration and broader consumer leverage concerns.
Rationale for large capital raise given current Tier 1 and profitability.
Impact of potential new insurance regulations on fee income.
Gold loan short-tenor schemes and competitive intensity.

delivery_comments.quote: Overall, I would say it is an excellent quarter with strong performance across all key metrics, of AUM, new customer addition, credit cost, profit growth, ROA and ROE.

These are fascinating numbers even for me, I would say. I didn't imagine we'll be growing quarterly between INR38,000 crores and INR39,000 crores on a run rate basis because that's been the case for the last two quarters now.
GNPA and NNPA of course, if first quarter -- first half is to go by, we remain pretty comfortably placed on credit quality at this point in time for FY27.

Thankfully, I would say it's still better than what we were originally estimated for months to that, I would just say it covered ground. June till June is looking much worse, quite honestly. So, coming in at 87% LPA is a much better number than it seemed as a 30-year biggest LNO.

delivery_comments.quote: The gold loan portfolio continued to witness strong momentum. It grew by 115%. The business now contributes to 3.5% overall AUM.
MSME continue to see muted growth. It grew by 6% only on account of a set of proactive risk actions that we have been taking since Q2 FY'26.
Cost of funds improved by 4 basis points in Q4 and came in at 7.41%. NIM remained steady.
Stage 2 and Stage 3 assets, just to give you a texture on credit quality, have sequentially reduced by INR 430-odd crores.
